messages.content:
Build an in-browser orbital mechanics simulator

Deliver a finished, usable product, not a demo page or marketing landing page. Choose the product concept, architecture, interactions, and visual direction yourself. Use actual orbital mechanics and state the model’s assumptions and limitations.

Make the product you think is most useful.

Runtime packaging and verification scaffold (separate from creative direction):
- Implement from scratch. Do not inspect the prior experiment, other runs, or any pre-existing simulator implementation. Do not delegate generation to another model.
- Work only in the supplied run directory. Create index.html with optional main.js and local CSS/JavaScript modules. If using main.js, HTML must contain exactly <script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>. CSS can be imported from main.js. A single fully inline HTML file is also allowed.
- Available environment: vanilla JavaScript, optional installed Three.js 0.186.1, Vite 7.3.6, Node 24. No additional dependencies, runtime network calls, remote assets/fonts, backend, accounts, analytics, or live orbital/celestial data. Do not modify package files or shared app files. Canvas, SVG, DOM, and 3D are all allowed; Three.js is not mandatory. If using WebGL, handle unsupported graphics gracefully.
- The common harness bundles JavaScript and CSS into one inline HTML document. Its viewer is an iframe sandbox with allow-scripts and an opaque origin. Do not access parent/top, communicate across frames, or rely on persistent storage, cookies, or origin-specific APIs.
- Make one bounded implementation and its self-test/repair phase. Validate JavaScript syntax and perform an isolated Vite build with write:false. Run quantitative numerical tests applicable to your chosen mechanics, independently of the interface, and preserve a directly rerunnable test script in the run directory. Test the actual implementation's physics functions, not a separately copied formula. Record exact commands, results, tolerances, and repairs. Repair your own implementation as needed for these checks. Do not impose a tiny arbitrary token cutoff or clone existing code.
- Browser localhost access is unavailable; do not claim browser checks or bypass that restriction. Actual browser appearance, interactions, and performance remain unverified until separately reviewed.
- Include worker-report.json with product title, description, implementation start/end UTC timestamps, exact tests and outcomes, numerical assumptions and limitations, repairs, and unknowns. Set tokenUsage and cost to null unless the runtime supplies measured values. Do not invent token counts, costs, or quality scores.

Reporting-only amendment (added after the first three launches; creative prompts and runtime constraints are unchanged):
At the end of your run, include actual runtime-provided token counters if accessible: input, cached input, output, reasoning, and total. Preserve the provider's field semantics and avoid double counting. Identify the counter source and whether counts include tools or agent overhead. Do not estimate from source length or the context budget, inspect restricted session-history paths, or inspect credentials. If actual counters are inaccessible, set tokenUsage to null and give the reason. Set cost to null unless measured cost is supplied by the runtime. Do not create another inference run solely to obtain counters.

suitesDetail.name: Circular orbit against analytic quarter-period solution and 1000-period return
Energy and angular momentum conservation over 600 actual propagated samples
Tangential/radial impulse magnitude and independent kinetic-energy increment
Hohmann transfers upward and downward reach target and circularize
Apsis timing reaches the expected extremum from an arbitrary epoch
Hyperbolic and near-parabolic propagation, including reverse-time recovery
Retrograde circular motion and local-tangential acceleration
Surface event timing for elliptic, hyperbolic, parabolic and radial infall
Projected ellipse matches both apsidal radii; invalid input is rejected

tests.name: Source-level interface orchestration audit
tests.method: Executes the actual main.js event handlers with lightweight Node DOM stubs; only the CSS import is omitted and the physics import location is adapted to a file URL. A test-only export exposes the existing orchestration functions without replacing them. This is not a browser check.
coverage: Invalid apsidal inputs leave mission intact
A 1,000,000-second jump stops at the first physical surface event to within 0.00001 km
Transfer departure, warp, arrival overshoot, exact arrival time, circularization, and summed delta-v
Transfer reset, manual cancellation, undo, and displayed warp synchronization

numericalModel.propagation: Keplerian universal-variable f/g propagation, Stumpff functions with a small-argument series, bracketed Newton iteration, and whole-period reduction for bounded elliptical trajectories.
numericalModel.burnDefinition: Instantaneous orthogonal local radial and local tangential velocity increments. Positive tangential follows the current angular-momentum direction; positive radial points away from Earth. Tangential is local-horizontal, not the full velocity-vector direction on an eccentric orbit.
numericalModel.collisionHandling: First future crossing of the mean spherical Earth surface is computed from the actual state. Simulation clamps to that time even when a warp step crosses an entire impact event.
numericalModel.transfer: Hohmann formulas for circular coplanar start and destination. The planner starts a fresh mission, executes departure, coasts for half of the transfer period, then executes arrival and pauses.
numericalModel.boundClassification: Reciprocal semimajor axis greater than 1e-14 km^-1 is treated as bound; the near-zero limit uses parabolic event timing.
assumptions: Fixed, spherical Earth and a negligible-mass spacecraft
Two-dimensional motion and a central inverse-square gravitational field
No atmosphere, drag, oblateness/J2, terrain, Sun/Moon perturbations, finite-duration thrust, propulsion/fuel constraints, or live ephemerides
Altitudes use the 6371 km mean spherical radius
GEO-class uses the conventional approximate 35786 km altitude and is not exactly sidereal with the chosen mean Earth radius; no rotating ground track is modeled
limitations: Educational two-body extrapolations are not mission predictions, especially at distant orbits or low altitude.
Next-apsis burn scheduling is offered for distinct apsides of bound ellipses; circular and unbound cases use current-position burns.
The orbit scrubber covers one period since the most recent orbital anchor; unbound trajectories use a 24-hour scrub window. Playback can continue beyond it.
Escape trajectory drawing is clipped to a finite radius while the physical propagation continues. A degenerate radial path has a schematic radial display.
Whole-orbit fitting can make Earth very small in an extremely extended orbit; Earth-focus, zoom, and pan controls provide a local view.
Hohmann is a standard fuel-efficient two-burn transfer, not a claim of global optimality for every radius ratio.
Each animation-frame wall-time increment is capped at 0.25 seconds to avoid a large background-tab catch-up.
State is session-only. Export provides manually selectable JSON and uses no origin-dependent clipboard, storage, or download API.

repairs.detail: Moved the automatic arrival undo snapshot before changing the prior-orbit comparison, so undo restores the original comparison state.
Synchronized the time-warp selector with the saved numerical warp on undo and restart.
Disabled next-apsis scheduling for circular and unbound cases without distinct supported apsides.
Made the no-Canvas fallback independent of the dynamic impact-warning banner, so normal telemetry updates cannot hide it.
Labeled the conventional approximate GEO altitude as GEO-class and disclosed its relationship to the chosen mean Earth radius.
Added Earth-focus alongside fit-orbit, zoom, and pan for highly extended trajectories.

unknowns: No browser or localhost checks were performed. Actual visual appearance, native browser DOM behavior, interactions, keyboard/screen-reader behavior, and performance remain unverified.
